title: ZenRail tessellation: workspace routing heuristics and compact dashboard rail
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design an alternative left-rail called 'ZenRail' that tessellates workspace tiles and routes to surface dashboards, rollout controls, and cost lenses with a compact footprint. This ticket covers heuristics for routing decisions, workspace switch affordances, and prototyping interaction patterns for dense multi-workspace customers. Goal is to reduce average route-switch time by 30% while preserving discoverability of rollouts and cost controls.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Prototype validated in moderated usability sessions with 8 participants, 2) Key routes (Dashboards, Rollouts, Cost Overview, Model Routes) accessible within 2 clicks for 95% of tasks, 3) Keyboard-first navigation flows and ARIA labels implemented in prototype, 4) Engineering has a clear routing map and component spec to implement incremental rollout.
design_notes:
- Introduce tessellated workspace chips grouped by role and recent activity.
- Each tile supports an overflow menu for workspace-level rollouts and cost toggle shortcuts.
- Secondary routes collapse into context clusters (Monitoring, Billing, Deployments) when viewport is < 1000px.
- Use progressive reveal: show primary icon+label on hover/focus, condensed icons only in compact mode.
- Maintain consistent route semantics with existing command palette and API endpoints.
- Ensure cost-lens CTA is present on dashboards at 3 density breakpoints.
decisions:
- Chose left-side Tessellation over top nav because vertical affordance allows quicker muscle memory for power users.
- Use hybrid routing: direct links for 6 highest-priority routes, cluster remaining routes into a contextual flyout.
- Workspace switcher becomes inline tile grid (not modal) to reduce context loss.
- Persist last-active route per-workspace to reduce cognitive load when switching.
tradeoffs:
- Density vs discoverability: compact mode improves vertical density for power users but hides less-used routes. Mitigation: persistent quick-search and command palette.
- Implementation complexity: per-workspace last-active-route requires backend state; agreed to implement optimistically on client with server sync later.
- Accessibility overhead: tessellated tiles require extra aria-describedby text; agreed to prioritise keyboard order and screen-reader labels over visual bells.
review_feedback: PM Claire O'Neill: prefer explicit billing shortcut in the overflow menu; concerned about discoverability on mobile.
Eng Lina Zhang: suggested server-side pin for last-active-route to avoid client drift; flagged potential perf cost for tile hydration.
Accessibility Sean O'Connor: requested clearer focus styles and linear DOM order for screen readers.
